content.text: Delete path works in staging; writing the dual-sign option as a follow-up so clients can opt into overlap.

After a webhook secret rotation, the X-Nimbus-Signature header continues to use the previous secret for roughly 30 seconds. Receivers that swapped to the new secret immediately reject those deliveries as invalid.

Expected: once rotation commits, new deliveries sign with the new secret; dual-sign (both secrets) may cover a short grace window if documented. Actual: a cache on the signing path keeps the old secret until its 30-second TTL expires, with no dual-sign.

Hypothesis: secret material is cached in the delivery worker with key sub:{id}:signing without a publish-time invalidation. Rotation updates Postgres but not the cache, so the worker keeps HMAC-ing with the stale value until TTL.
Security-conscious customers who rotate after a leak see a burst of signature failures and may disable the subscription.
